item.title: Re: Video Games
item.content:encoded:
Warcraft: The Burning Legion and The Frozen Throne are absolute bombs. I have many fond and nostalgic memories from playing those games.

Other than that, I used to play a lot of flash games (yes, I'm a zoomer) but I've since outgrown them. One of those great flash games that I played religiously was the Epic Battle Fantasy series which parodied RPG games but mostly parodied Final Fantasy.

Nowadays, I prefer to play those clicker incremental games primarily because I'm not too invested in playing flash games as much as I used to. I get bored pretty quick playing video games once I finish them :/

I am, however, waiting patiently for Watch_Dogs Legion. That's the game that I'll sell myself out for.

item.title: Re: Video Games
item.content:encoded:
If forced to pick a single all-time favorite game, I pretty much always reply with Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. The silver and bronze medals go to Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time and the original Mass Effect.

Over the course of the last year and a half, though, I've gotten ridiculously hooked on the Monster Hunter series. From a free toss-in game at a local GameStop, I've now logged something like five hundred hours of play across three different titles.

item.title: Re: Video Games
item.content:encoded:
My favorite game of all time is Fallout New Vegas. I hadn't really thought about it this way until just now, but on top of having an excellent interactive story and characters and world, it also let me get at aspects of the games I loved playing while I was growing up. See, I was deeply into the Half-Life mod community for many years (especially single-player/story mods), and Fallout 2 was amazing, so a Fallout 2 sequel (literally and tonally, unlike 3) + shooters + mods… It's kinda got everything.

(If anyone hasn't played Half-Life, go play Black Mesa.)

I also enjoy games I can just zone out to while listening to podcasts. I used to play a lot of Viscera Cleanup Detail, and there's an old shovelware game called Hard Truck: Apocalypse that, like, I could just play forever. Also an old game called Enclave that I keep going back to.

Also, I cheat *constantly*. I hate rogue-likes and rogue-lites for the most part, but I'll still play through them if I can cheat out the more pointlessly frustrating elements. (If I want pointless frustration, I'll play Viscera Cleanup Detail or Mudrunner or something.)

item.title: Re: Video Games
item.content:encoded:
I'm particularly interested in games that has an open world and building mechanics where you can explore and build to your heart's content.
The most obvious title is Minecraft, I've been playing it since 2014. there is just something about the game that just draws your attention, you know what I mean? Like its a game of infinite possibilities and creativity that's why I played it.
Another game you guys may have heard about is unturned, I know what you guys are thinking;"unturned is just a minecraft/roblox knockoff". Unturned start off as a game on roblox, but the dev got tired of the system and people copying his game so he remade the game entirly and is now one of the more popular free game on steam. With you exploring the map and raiding bases, there is almost nothing you can't do in unturned.
